evidence.detail: Sanitize deck export filenames — changed file_name() regex from stripping only colons to stripping all non-[0-9a-z-] characters after anyascii conversion, guaranteeing ASCII-only output in the Content-Disposition filename
Earlier partial fix: added anyascii() to file_name() to transliterate non-ASCII to ASCII before stripping
Current code: re.sub('[^0-9a-z-]', '', anyascii(safe_name), flags=re.IGNORECASE) — produces only [0-9a-zA-Z-] characters, always Latin1-safe in HTTP headers

triage.notes: The earlier fix (2a51b7ae / PR #13501) only stripped colons; commit 48e99b21 completed the fix by stripping all non-[0-9a-z-] characters.
triage.proposed_comment: This was fixed by commit 48e99b21 (Aug 2026), which changed `file_name()` to strip all non-alphanumeric/hyphen characters (via `re.sub('[^0-9a-z-]', '', anyascii(safe_name))`) after an earlier partial fix (commit 2a51b7ae) added `anyascii` transliteration. The export filename is now guaranteed to be ASCII-safe.

verify.final_comment: Fixed by commit 48e99b21, which tightened the file_name() regex from stripping only colons to stripping all characters not in [0-9a-z-] after anyascii transliteration (building on the earlier partial fix in 2a51b7ae). The export filename is now guaranteed to be ASCII-safe and valid in HTTP headers.

own_evidence.detail: Current file_name() runs re.sub('[^0-9a-z-]', '', anyascii(safe_name)), stripping all non-ASCII and non-alphanumeric-hyphen characters, guaranteeing a latin1-safe Content-Disposition filename.
Diff shows the prior regex re.sub(':', '', ...) only stripped colons; the new regex strips all characters outside [0-9a-z-], closing the remaining encoding gap.
